ai.literal: Glory to a person is the wealth of determination; disgrace to a person is thinking 'we shall live' having lost that.
ai.translation: A person's glory is the wealth of their inner determination; their disgrace is thinking, 'We shall live on,' after having lost that determination.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்குப் பெருமை என்பது அவனது ஊக்கமாகிய செல்வமே ஆகும்; அவனுக்கு இழிவு என்பது அந்த ஊக்கத்தை இழந்துவிட்டும் 'நாம் உயிர் வாழ்வோம்' என்று நினைப்பதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true greatness and disgrace through the lens of inner strength. Glory is described as the wealth of determination that a person possesses. In contrast, disgrace is the attitude of wanting to live on after losing that noble determination. The poet suggests that a life devoid of high aspirations and self-respect is a shameful existence, whereas a life driven by strong willpower is truly glorious.

ai.literal: Birth is equal to all living beings; distinction is not alike because of the differences in deeds done.
ai.translation: All living beings are equal by birth; their distinctions arise only from the differences in the deeds they perform.
ai.modern: எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் பிறப்பு என்பது சமமானது; ஆனால் அவர்கள் செய்யும் செயல்களின் வேறுபாடுகளால் அவர்களுக்குரிய சிறப்புகள் சமமாவதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes the fundamental equality of all living beings at the moment of birth. While birth is a common, equalizing factor for everyone, true greatness or distinction is not inherent or predetermined. Instead, individuals are distinguished solely by the quality and nature of the actions they perform throughout their lives. Thus, one's worth is defined by their deeds, not by their birth.

ai.literal: Even though being in a high position, those who do not have noble character are not noble; even though being in a low position, those who do not have base character are not base.
ai.translation: Even when placed in high positions, those who lack noble qualities are never noble; and even when placed in low positions, those who lack base qualities are never base.
ai.modern: உயர்ந்த நிலையில் இருந்தாலும், மேன்மையான குணம் இல்லாதவர்கள் மேலானவர்கள் அல்லர்; தாழ்ந்த நிலையில் இருந்தாலும், இழிவான குணம் இல்லாதவர்கள் தாழ்ந்தவர்கள் அல்லர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that true greatness or baseness is determined solely by one's character, not by social status or position. The poet uses the words 'mēl' (high/noble) and 'kīḻ' (low/base) in two distinct senses: physical or social position, and moral character. A person of low character does not become noble simply by being elevated to a high position. Conversely, a person of noble character does not become base even when forced into a lowly position.

ai.literal: Like women of single-minded chastity, greatness also, if one conducts oneself maintaining oneself, exists.
ai.translation: Just like women of single-minded chastity, greatness exists only when a person guards and conducts themselves with self-discipline.
ai.modern: ஒருமைப்பாடு உடைய கற்புடைய பெண்களைப் போல, பெருமை என்னும் பண்பும் ஒருவன் தன்னைத் தானே காத்துக் கொண்டு ஒழுக்கத்தோடு வாழ்ந்தால் தான் நிலைபெற்று இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the preservation of personal greatness to the single-minded chastity of virtuous women. The word 'orumaic' refers to singleness of mind, which represents unwavering fidelity and self-control. The poet explains that greatness is not a permanent birthright; it only exists if a person actively guards their own character and conducts themselves with discipline. Just as a chaste woman protects her virtue, an individual must constantly guard their integrity to maintain true greatness.

ai.literal: Greatness those-who-possess will-accomplish by-the-proper-way difficulty possessing deeds.
ai.translation: Those who possess true greatness will accomplish, by the proper means, deeds of rare difficulty.
ai.modern: பெருமைப் பண்பு உடையவர்கள், செய்வதற்கு அரிய செயல்களையும் உரிய நல்வழியில் செய்து முடிப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the capability and methodology of noble individuals. Those who possess greatness of character (பெருமை உடையவர்) do not shy away from difficult tasks; they successfully perform (ஆற்றுவார்) deeds of rare difficulty (அருமை உடைய செயல்). Crucially, they do so 'ஆற்றின்'—meaning by the right path, method, or righteous means. Their greatness is defined not just by the magnitude of their achievements, but by their adherence to proper principles while achieving them.

ai.literal: Within the mind of the small-minded, there is not the outlook that says, 'We will cherish and adopt the great'.
ai.translation: The attitude of wanting to cherish and align oneself with great minds does not exist within the consciousness of the small-minded.
ai.modern: சிறிய குணம் உடையவர்களின் மனத்தில், பெரியவர்களைப் போற்றிப் பாராட்டிக் கொள்வோம் என்னும் நோக்கம் இருப்பதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the small-minded (சிறியார்) with the truly great (பெரியார்). It states that those of low character lack the mental capacity or attitude (நோக்கு) to appreciate and cherish the great. The word 'உணர்ச்சி' refers to their inner consciousness or perception, which is too narrow to harbor the noble aspiration of seeking the company and guidance of the wise. Because of their limited vision, they never think of honoring or learning from those who are superior in character.

ai.literal: Indeed excess practiced nature-of-action becomes even distinction itself, excellence with-those-who-lack if-obtained.
ai.translation: If high status and distinction are acquired by those who lack excellent qualities, it will only result in actions of sheer arrogance and excess.
ai.modern: சிறந்த பண்புகள் இல்லாதவர்களிடம் உயர்வோ சிறப்போ வந்து சேர்ந்தால், அது வரம்பு மீறிய செயல்களைச் செய்யும் தன்மையுடையதாகவே மாறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how power or high status affects people of different characters. The word 'சீர்' refers to excellent qualities or merit, and 'அல்லவர்' refers to those who lack them. When 'சிறப்பு' (distinction, wealth, or high status) reaches such unworthy people, it does not make them noble. Instead, it manifests as 'இறப்பு' (excessiveness or arrogance) in their actions ('தொழிற்று'). The poet warns that giving power to those without character only leads to the transgression of limits and harmful behavior.

ai.literal: Greatness will indeed always bow; smallness will indeed adorn itself admiring itself.
ai.translation: Greatness always behaves with humility; smallness, however, adorns itself with self-admiration.
ai.modern: பெருமைக்குரிய பண்பு எப்போதும் பணிவோடு நடக்கும்; ஆனால் சிறுமையான பண்பு தன்னைத்தானே வியந்து பாராட்டிப் பெருமைப்படுத்திக் கொள்ளும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the behavior of truly noble minds with that of small-minded people. Greatness (பெருமை) is characterized by constant humility (பணியுமாம் என்றும்); those who are truly great do not boast but remain humble. In contrast, smallness of character (சிறுமை) is marked by self-admiration (தன்னை வியந்து), where such individuals constantly praise themselves and metaphorically 'adorn' themselves with vanity (அணியுமாம்). The particle 'ஆம்' in both verbs emphasizes that these are natural, observable truths of human behavior.

ai.literal: Greatness is the absence of self-importance; pettiness is riding on self-importance.
ai.translation: Greatness is characterized by the absence of self-importance; pettiness is marked by riding high on pride.
ai.modern: பெருமை என்பது அகந்தை இல்லாமல் இருப்பது ஆகும்; சிறுமை என்பது அகந்தையைத் தலைமேல் ஏற்றி வைத்துக் கொண்டு ஆடுவது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts true greatness with pettiness. Greatness is defined not by power or wealth, but by the complete absence of self-importance or arrogance ('perumitam'). Conversely, pettiness is marked by riding upon pride, letting arrogance drive one's actions. The verb 'ūrntu' (riding or mounting) vividly illustrates how petty minds are carried away by their own inflated self-worth.

ai.literal: Vulnerability hides greatness; pettiness indeed faults only speaking will-do.
ai.translation: Greatness of character covers up the vulnerabilities of others, whereas pettiness does nothing but broadcast their faults.
ai.modern: பெருந்தன்மை பிறருடைய பலவீனங்களை மறைக்கும்; ஆனால் சிறுமைக்குணம் பிறருடைய குற்றங்களை மட்டுமே பிறருக்குச் சொல்லிக்கொண்டே இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the behavior of noble and petty minds. A person of greatness (perumai) possesses the magnanimity to shield and conceal the vulnerabilities or private weaknesses (aṟṟam) of others. On the other hand, a petty person (siṟumai) actively seeks out and broadcasts only the flaws (kuṟṟam) of others. The contrast highlights that nobility protects others' dignity, while pettiness thrives on exposing their shortcomings.
